schema_conformance.note: The same seam every observation in this series records: contracts/participant-observation.schema.json sets additionalProperties false and admits none of the six top-level fields the landing gate reads.

method.independence: Read a read-only worktree detached at the pinned commit; git status --porcelain empty at the start and end of the reading. Nothing in the subject tree was edited; mutations were applied to scratch copies.
own_method: Pinned the subject and confirmed the tree did not move underneath the reading.
Derived scope from git diff --name-status against the base rather than from the declared file list.
Ran verify.py and lint.py from the pinned checkout, recording each command's own exit code.
Ran all 55 corpus mutations and collected every violation emitted, then compared that set against every refusal message the package states, to find refusals no case fires.
Constructed adversarial dispatches and re-ran both named test modules on each.
Measured derives_from_agent_result on the pristine tree to test the resolver in the other direction.

observed.undeclared_note: The account said two new test modules; four are added. sov-epic.js and sov-coldstart.js carry syntax repairs beyond the demotion sentence the account describes.
observed.overclaim: 'the other 21 carry a demotion sentence ahead of what they splice' is false as measured. Of 28 non-frame witness dispatches, three carry no demotion sentence at all because they splice nothing, and two splice a repository path or a constant ahead of the sentence. Harmless in substance; the sentence as written is not what the artifact does.

defeats.shows: `agent` reached under another name, so the provenance reader sees nothing.
defeats.mechanism: bindings.AGENT_CALL matched the literal `agent(`. calls._agent_names already resolved aliases to a fixpoint for enumeration, and the provenance resolver was never given the same resolution.
defeats.mutation: A workflow with `const spawn = agent`, a build dispatched through `spawn(...)`, and a witness prompt splicing `built.summary` as its oracle. `agent.call(null, ...)` defeats it identically.
defeats.result: violations() returned [] across all 23 workflows; both named test modules OK. derives_from_agent_result(src, 'built.summary') returned False.

defeats.shows: The frame's subject pin deleted from what the evaluator receives, with the real frame left in place as dead code.
defeats.mechanism: _frame_violations grades `function witnessFrame(`; _dispatch_violations keyed the frame path on `witnessFrame(` appearing in masked text, while test_witness_context_provenance asserted the same thing over raw source. A comment `/* witnessFrame( */` satisfies one grader and not the other. The position rule is separately zeroed: with the label as the first literal, the count of markers before it is 0, so no expression is ever asked about.
defeats.mutation: A helper `witnessBrief` returning joined blocks that tell the evaluator not to pin and to take the builder's scope as given, spliced where the frame was, behind a leading demotion sentence and a `/* witnessFrame( */` comment.
defeats.result: violations({'sov-loop.js': src}) == []; both named test modules OK. Full verify.py output byte-identical to the unmutated control.

defeats.shows: The provenance resolver fires on schema literals, in the other direction.
defeats.mechanism: The binding map read an object literal's `key: value` pairs as bindings of `key`, so a JSON Schema's property names walked to whatever they collided with.
defeats.measurement: On the pristine tree, derives_from_agent_result returned True for BUILD_SCHEMA, WITNESS_SCHEMA and residuals in sov-asset.js; the chain was built -> results -> thunks -> BUILD_SCHEMA -> residuals -> witness -> agent(.
defeats.result: Refusal messages annotated 'provenance to an agent result is measurable' were name collisions. render.py's own standard - a check that convicts correct code is worse than the gap it covers - was not met.

residuals: One refusal has no corpus case that fires it: the prompt_of / Unreadable branch reached when a witness call does not have exactly two arguments. Every other refusal in the package fires on at least one case.
`expects` is matched by substring, and 'what this prompt delivers cannot be read' is emitted verbatim from two different branches, so a case could migrate between them and still pass.
Coverage is lopsided: 16 of 55 cases fire the single 'no label demoting the builder's account' refusal, while the position rule has exactly one case.
The subject pin is required only of a file declaring `function witnessFrame(`. Twenty-two of twenty-three workflows have no subject-pin requirement at all.
The two test modules and audit.violations are not the same oracle: the provenance test greps raw source where the audit grades rendered text. G2 lives in that gap.
escaped_agent_references returns on the first `eval`, discarding every other escape in the file.
observation_basis is honest and its docstring matches, but the RESOLVED half rests on a caller-set boolean the kernel cannot check, and the vocabulary did not follow the rename into the test names.
lexer.py records in its own comment that two scanners in the package genuinely disagree and that their both failing closed is luck rather than design. Unrepaired.
corpus_reading: All 55 cases produced at least one violation containing their own expects string, measured rather than read off the test. Thirteen fire additional refusals beyond their declared one; none passes only on an unrelated violation.
judgement_items: Is a mechanism that enforces the subject pin on one of twenty-three workflow files, and presence-of-a-sentence on the other twenty-two, an admissible reading of Release gate 6, or does the gate require the frame to be the only way to construct a witness prompt?

Does a landing ledger field named observation_basis: SUPPLIED_AND_RESOLVED, whose RESOLVED half is asserted by the calling tool rather than established by the kernel, satisfy the standing grant's independent-observation precondition?
standing_reason: The claim's central invariant - that the package grades every witness dispatch against Release gate 6 - is defeated by two independent constructions with verify, lint and both test modules green. OPEN -> BUILT is also declined: the artifact exists but the claim made about it does not hold. A narrower claim about the module as code could support it.
